title: Ordinary ice-bearing dust needs at least 1.11 mag of r attenuation to match the reported 2025 band of Gaia20cdd under the tested covering model
abstract: We test whether arbitrary partial cover by ordinary ice-bearing dust can match the reported 2025 3.1 um band of Gaia20cdd and its shallow optical deficit. An analytic mixture bound and numerical checks give a minimum total r attenuation of 1.114 mag for band depth 0.33 with the stated Taurus slope and no ice threshold. The reported deficit is 0.153 mag. A broad parameter test gives a minimum of 0.740 mag. Thus cloud cover alone fails if the quiet optical level is unobscured and the band comes from the same stellar source. A general opacity bound requires at least one sightline to have an ice-to-extinction coefficient above 23 times the Taurus value for the nominal inputs. Persistent obscuration of at least 0.961 mag in the quiet state can remove the nominal exclusion. We provide a proof, code, model tables, sensitivity tests and source hashes. This is a conditional analysis of published measurements, not a new detection. Stellar brightness weights, continuum error, source mixing and non-simultaneous observations remain limitations.

display.caption: Minimum total r attenuation for an arbitrary distribution of dust columns. The comparison with the quiet-state deficit requires an unobscured quiet reference.
